claims.text: An ML interatomic potential trained on a broad range of ab initio liquid configurations will capture multicomponent HEA interactions and configurational diversity better than EAM references.
The proposed ML-IP will improve phase-space overlap with the ab initio target.
The proposed ML-IP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The relevant initial systems are multicomponent HEAs in liquid and solid states at or near their melting temperatures.
The ML-IP should be trained on extensive high-temperature ab initio molecular-dynamics data from both liquid and solid phases.
The method applies to HEAs containing five or more principal elements.
The applicable high-temperature range is approximately above 0.9 times the melting temperature.
Atomic configurational diversity is most pronounced near or at the melting point.
A machine-learned many-body functional form represents instantaneous atomic environments and configurational space more accurately than the fixed EAM functional form.
Training on configurations spanning the ab initio liquid enables improved reference-target phase-space overlap.
Representing configurational fluctuations in both liquid and solid states reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will decrease by on the order of tens of percent relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Improvement will be observable as better agreement between the reference and target free-energy landscapes.
TOR-TILD's EAM references inadequately represent the configurational diversity of the ab initio liquid.
The approach should be most effective for equimolar or near-equimolar HEAs near their melting temperatures.
Performance under extreme compositional imbalance or far outside the training regime is uncertain.
ML-IP successes in simpler elemental or binary systems indicate that such potentials can capture complex interactions.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction in multicomponent HEAs will vary with the quality and configurational range of the training data.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing EAM- and ML-IP-referenced thermodynamic integration for the same solid and liquid HEAs near melting.
Failure to achieve a tens-of-percent reduction in path mismatch, or failure to improve phase-space-overlap metrics, will falsify the hypothesis.
